new_statements.quote: Crowley & Bowern 2010, Ex. 15: "15 NYULNYULAN (WESTERN AUSTRALIA) (Stress is on the initial syllable of all words in all languages; rr is a trill; r is a glide; y is used for the palatal glide. Otherwise the transcriptions are in IPA ..." [Google Books snippet text]. Nekes & Worms 2006:67: "1.4. Accentuation The main accent of a word usually falls on the first syllable, as in the Nyulnyul examples bádang 'stick', bádang-an (stick-with) 'with a stick' and yámendedjalen 'I awake'. However, a slight secondary accent is sometimes heard on the fourth syllable of the word yámendedjàlen. Another example illustrating secondary accent is provided by the Nyikina mindenàno 'you told me', with secondary accent on the third syllable" [assembled from overlapping snippets].

Nimanburru Yawuru Nyikina a:mba wamb wa:mba wamba wamba 'man'", so Nimanburru is indeed one of the exercise's languages. No page number is vis…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress on the first syllable of every word (Crowley & Bowern, for all the Nyulnyulan languages in their data set including Nimanburru); Nekes & Worms give the same first-syllable rule for the Dampier Land languages they recorded, with occasional exceptions marked by diacritics.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nekes & Worms 2006:67: a slight secondary accent sometimes on the fourth syllable (Nyulnyul yámendedjàlen) or third syllable (Nyikina mindenàno). Crowley & Bowern: not mentioned.
new_statements.exceptions: Nekes & Worms: 'usually' on the first syllable; 'a few exceptions' are marked with grave and acute diacritics (per the snippet 'accentuation explained in the introduction. In these few exceptions we employ the usage of grave and acute diacritics, as proposed by the Smithsonian Institute'); the orthography section mentions a case where the stress is on the second syllable (context not recoverable from the snippet). Crowley & Bowern: none.
new_statements.domain_note: Crowley & Bowern: word level, a blanket note over all six Nyulnyulan languages in a textbook comparative-reconstruction exercise (Bowern is the only linguist to have transcribed the Nimanburru tapes). Nekes & Worms p. 67: word-level 'main accent', generalised over the Dampier Land dialects they recorded, illustrated with Nyulnyul (and Nyikina) examples, not Nimanburru ones.
new_statements.identity_note: Nimanburru = nima1245 (ISO nmp, AIATSIS K9), Western Nyulnyulan, eastern Dampier Peninsula; extinct (Peile's 1960s tapes are the last recordings). Nekes & Worms 2006 treat it as one of the 'Dampier Land dialects' alongside Nyulnyul (nyul1247), Jabirrjabirr (dyab1238) and Bardi (bard1255); their accentuation statement is illustrated with Nyulnyul (nyul1247) and Nyikina (nyig1240) forms, not Nimanburru ones. Crowley & Bowern's exercise note covers Nimanburru explicitly together with Bardi, Nyulnyul, Jabirrjabirr, Yawuru and Nyikina.
